title: The Fox and the Grapes

full_text:
On a sweltering summer afternoon, a sly fox strolled through an orchard bathed in warm sunlight. His throat was parched, and his stomach rumbled with hunger. As he reached a high garden wall, his amber eyes caught sight of a magnificent grapevine that wound its way along a tall wooden trellis. Hanging overhead were rich, luscious clusters of dark purple grapes, glistening with delicate drops of morning dew and bursting with sweet, cool juice.

The fox licked his whiskers and grinned. "Here is a feast fit for an emperor," he muttered, stepping back a few paces to gain momentum. With a graceful leap, he sprang high into the air with jaws wide open, but his teeth snapped on empty air, missing the lowest bunch by mere inches.

Refusing to admit defeat, the fox backed up further into the dusty furrow, gathered all his strength, and sprang upward once more. Again he fell short, tumbling onto the soft earth. Three, four, five times he leaped, straining every muscle in his russet body until his breath came in ragged wheezes and his legs trembled with exhaustion.

Looking up at the purple prize that hung tantalizingly out of reach, the fox curled his snout into an arrogant sneer. He brushed the dust from his bushy tail and announced loudly to the listening birds: "Why should I waste my precious energy on such wretched fruit? I can see plainly from here that they are completely green and sour, unfit for a gentleman's palate!" And with his head held high in pretended disgust, he trotted away through the briers.
moral: It is easy to despise and pretend to scorn what you cannot possess.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Fox and the Grapes"?
options: It is easy to despise what you cannot get.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
